mmx6-v0.1.0.description:
First release: Mega Man X6 (PS1, NTSC-U, SLUS-01395) as an Archipelago
multiworld game — an apworld for generation and a BizHawk-based client for
play. The patch is produced from your own verified dump at patch time; two
dumps are accepted (Redump **Mega Man X6 (USA) (Rev 1)** and one known
development dump). The setup guide inside the apworld walks through
everything, including verifying your disc.

## What it plays like

- **Goal:** beat all eight Mavericks, then the endgame. The Gate's Lab stays
  shut until the eighth is down — vanilla opens it early off High Max, and the
  client closes that route off until you are actually done.
- **29 base locations** (bosses, Heart Tanks, capsules, sub-tanks), plus **128
  Reploid rescues** and **3 endgame clears** on by default.
- **QoL on by default:** dialogue appears instantly and advances itself, intro
  videos are skipped, the pause menu offers Exit Stage from the start, and
  Reploids grabbed by a Nightmare are never lost for good.
- **Optional:** stage unlocks as items, Zero unlock, armor parts in the pool,
  secret armors in the pool, boss HP randomization, weapon damage
  randomization.

## What to watch in this first release

Stated so nobody has to guess what was and was not seen running:

- **`protect_reploids` is verified at the instruction level, not
  behaviourally.** All three patched routines read back patched in live RAM,
  but nobody has yet watched a Nightmare reach a Reploid and the Reploid
  survive it. If you lose a Reploid with the option on, that is a bug report
  we want.
- **The eight special-weapon item names came from a written guide** and have
  not all been checked against the in-game weapon-get text, so a name may
  differ slightly from what the game shows.
- **Zero's weapon gauge is written but its bar has not been watched.** X's
  gauges and Zero's life gauge are confirmed live; if Zero's weapon bar draws
  wrong after an upgrade, say so.
- **Reaching the ending early is remembered only until the client restarts.**
  If you see the ending short of eight Mavericks, finish the rest, but the
  client reconnected in between, the goal will not fire until you go through
  the endgame once more. Worst case is a second Sigma fight, not a broken
  seed.

---

`mmx6.apworld` goes in your Archipelago install's `custom_worlds/` folder.
`MMX6-Unpatcher.exe` restores an AP-patched disc to a clean dump if you have
lost your original — drag a `.bin` onto it.

Requires Archipelago 0.6.7 or newer. 311 tests, release gate 79/79.

mmx6-v0.1.1.description:
Bugfix release, prompted by the first wave of tester reports on v0.1.0. Thank
you Icey, Batter the Beast and Sanae — all three reports were real, and two
were seed-breaking.

## Do these two things

- **RE-PATCH YOUR DISC.** Two fixes change the disc patch, so updating the
  apworld alone is not enough: install the new `mmx6.apworld`, patch a clean
  dump again through Open Patch, and play the new `.bin`.
- **REGENERATE seeds that were generated on 0.1.0.** Two fixes are logic
  bugs — the 0.1.0 generator placed items on wrong assumptions, and no
  re-patch can move them. A `stage_unlocks` seed whose only Nightmare-wall
  opener is Shield Sheldon is unwinnable until regenerated.

## Fixed

- **An unkillable boss under `boss_hp_randomization`** *(re-patch)*.
  Nightmare Pressure's HP was written to two disc sites, and only one is HP —
  the other drives the fight's scripted transition, so rolling it left the
  boss invulnerable after its parts died. The release gate now disassembles
  every boss-HP site and requires the life-bar store nearby, with the bad
  site kept as a negative control, so a lookalike byte cannot get in again.
- **The Nightmare wall opens on Fire only** *(regenerate)*. Both Fire
  (Heatnix) and Mirror (Sheldon) can afflict North Pole, but only Fire opens
  the fire-room wall — Mirror leaves it shut and overwrites Fire on top.
  Logic now requires Blaze Heatnix beaten, and his Access Codes under
  `stage_unlocks`.
- **Reploids have logic rules now** *(regenerate)*. A full roster of all 128
  ended the "nobody knows which of a stage's sixteen sits where" era: 40
  Reploids now inherit the rule of the pickup they stand beside — the
  fire-room seven in North Pole, the high-ledge and Another Route groups
  elsewhere — and only where that pickup was already gated.
- **The endgame gate stops fighting the game** *(client only)*. The game
  opens Gate's Lab on its own at 3000 Nightmare Souls or on beating High Max
  in an Another Route; the 0.1.0 client wrote it shut, the game re-opened it
  every stage exit, and the unlock cutscene replayed forever while the Gate
  stayed enterable anyway. The client now acts only on a Maverick count read
  on a screen it trusts, corrects the byte at most three times, then stops
  and warns you plainly **not to fight Sigma yet**. It says so again — "the
  Gate is open" — when the eighth Maverick falls, and no longer scolds a
  player who is legitimately inside the endgame at 8/8.
- **`zero_unlock`'s description tells the truth**: beating the Zero Nightmare
  (the first Another Route boss) makes Zero playable with no item involved,
  exactly as in vanilla. The option gates Zero only if you leave Another
  Routes alone; logic never assumes the shortcut, so nothing strands either
  way.

## What to watch in this release

- The endgame-gate concession is built from one tester's report and unit
  tests; the concede threshold has not been watched live. If you see the
  **DO NOT FIGHT SIGMA YET** warning, heed it — and tell us.
- The Reploid gating derives from a community roster cross-checked against
  our own captures; fine positions are still guide-sourced. A Reploid the
  tracker calls reachable that you provably cannot reach (or the reverse) is
  a wanted report — name the stage and Reploid number.

---

`mmx6.apworld` goes in your Archipelago install's `custom_worlds/` folder.
`MMX6-Unpatcher.exe` restores an AP-patched disc to a clean dump if you have
lost your original — drag a `.bin` onto it.

Requires Archipelago 0.6.7 or newer. 317 tests, release gate 82/82.

All MMX6 releases: https://github.com/Shinnuu/Archipelago/releases?q=mmx6

mmx6-v0.2.0.description:
Feature release: four new options, player colours, and the endgame gate fixed
on the disc instead of fought over by the client.

## Do this first

- **REGENERATE your seeds to get the endgame fix.** It is per-seed disc data,
  baked into the `.apmmx6` when the seed is generated, so re-opening a 0.1.1
  patch file cannot deliver it. Seeds generated on 0.1.1 are not broken —
  they stay winnable and keep the old client-side gate — but the Gate can
  still open early on them.
- **If you use player colours, use THIS release's `MMX6-Unpatcher.exe`.**
  The 0.1.1 one refuses a recoloured disc.

## Fixed

- **The endgame opens on eight Mavericks and nothing else** *(regenerate)*.
  Under `all_mavericks`, vanilla could still open Gate's Lab early — on 3000
  Nightmare Souls, or by beating High Max in an Another Route — and the
  client could not hold it shut: it wrote the byte closed, the game wrote it
  open again on the next stage exit, and the unlock cutscene replayed every
  stage. The disc now switches both early openings off where the game decides
  them, in eight one-immediate edits. Verified live with a control: on an
  unpatched disc 3500 Souls at 2/8 opened the Gate; on the patched disc the
  same steps left it shut with no cutscene. Not applied under the `sigma`
  goal, where opening on Souls is the game's own design. The client still
  opens the Gate itself at 8/8 as a backstop.

## New

- **`disabled_nightmare_effects`** — switch Nightmare Effects off, named one
  at a time in any combination, or `all`. Case does not matter. Each stage
  can be afflicted by exactly two of the eight, so turning one off does not
  clear a stage by itself. Turning **Fire** off puts nothing important behind
  North Pole's ice wall: the nine locations behind it are excluded and hold
  junk, and the patch also tries to hold the wall open so they stay
  collectable. Souls get much harder to farm with effects off; nothing here
  needs them.
- **`scaravich_no_progression`** — every location in Central Museum holds
  junk, so nothing you need is behind the random totem-pole rooms. The checks
  still send; they are just never worth re-rolling for. Also stops the client
  holding the Blade Armor Helmet back until that capsule is found.
- **`starting_hp`** (1–127, vanilla 32) and **`heart_tank_value`** (0–64,
  vanilla 2) — the life X and Zero start with, and how much each Heart Tank
  or Life Up is worth. 127 is the game's own ceiling. Every value plays,
  checked live; the bar just draws as a stub below 32 and stays the 64 size
  above it. The starting value is baked into the seed; the gauge is written
  absolutely, so a Heart Tank whose item went elsewhere gives you no +2.
- **Player colours** — X, Zero, Shadow, Blade and Ultimate Armor, 18 presets
  or `random`, set in your own `host.yaml` under `mmx6_options` and applied
  when the patch is opened. Changing one is a re-patch of the same
  `.apmmx6`, never a regeneration; delete the old `.bin`/`.cue` first or the
  patcher skips its work. **Falcon Armor and Black Zero are not covered** —
  and X6 starts you in Falcon, so `x_palette` shows once you are plain X or
  have switched armours. Details in the setup guide.

## What to watch in this release

- **The eighth-Maverick unlock itself has not yet been observed on a patched
  disc.** The client opens the Gate on the next stage select regardless, but
  if your Gate does not appear after the eighth Maverick, please say so.
- Disabling Nightmare effects does **not** clear effects a save already
  holds; the stage select simply stops assigning new ones.

---

`mmx6.apworld` goes in your Archipelago install's `custom_worlds/` folder.
`MMX6-Unpatcher.exe` restores an AP-patched disc (recoloured or not) to a
clean dump if you have lost your original — drag a `.bin` onto it.
`MMX6-Setup-Guide.pdf` is the setup guide, readable before anything is
installed.

Requires Archipelago 0.6.7 or newer. 488 tests, release gate 102/102,
packaged e2e 15/15.

mmx6-v0.2.1.description:
**Player colours move into your YAML.**

0.2.0 put them in `host.yaml`, and the feedback was consistent: people did not
want to edit a file they had never opened, and several never found out the
feature existed at all — `host.yaml` settings do not appear on the website
generator.

So the five colours (X, Zero, Shadow, Blade and Ultimate) are ordinary options
now. They show up on the generator with everything else, a typo is refused when
the seed is generated instead of quietly falling back to vanilla, and your
colour is recorded in the spoiler.

## Nothing breaks, and nothing needs regenerating

- **A colour already set in `host.yaml` keeps working exactly as before.** It
  is an override now, and it still wins.
- **YAMLs written for 0.2.0 still generate.** The new options default to
  vanilla.
- You only need a new seed if you want your colour to come from the YAML.
  Anyone mid-seed can keep changing colours by re-patching, as now.

## Two details worth knowing

`random` is rolled when the seed is generated now, rather than from your player
name. Your colour is fixed and appears in the spoiler. It picks from the whole
list, so it can land on vanilla.

**`vanilla` in `host.yaml` does not override anything.** It means "nothing set
here". Archipelago writes those entries into your `host.yaml` by itself with
`vanilla` already in them, so honouring it as a real choice would have quietly
overridden the YAML of every existing player. To play in vanilla colours, pick
`vanilla` in your YAML.

Falcon Armor and Black Zero are still not covered and keep their usual colours.

---

Everything from 0.2.0 still applies if you are coming from 0.1.1 — the endgame
gate fix needs a **regenerated** seed, and the four options added there are
unchanged. See the
[0.2.0 notes](https://github.com/Shinnuu/Archipelago/releases/tag/mmx6-v0.2.0).

`mmx6.apworld` goes in your Archipelago install's `custom_worlds/` folder.
`MMX6-Unpatcher.exe` restores an AP-patched disc (recoloured or not) to a clean
dump if you have lost your original — drag a `.bin` onto it. It is unchanged
from 0.2.0 and you do not need to replace it.
`MMX6-Setup-Guide.pdf` is the setup guide, readable before anything is
installed.

Requires Archipelago 0.6.7 or newer. 511 tests, release gate 102/102,
packaged e2e 15/15.

All MMX6 releases: https://github.com/Shinnuu/Archipelago/releases?q=mmx6

mmx6-v0.3.0.description:
Four changes from the first X5+X6 multiworld. Two are disc changes and one is a
logic change, so read the last section before updating mid-seed.

## Fixed: a seed could be unwinnable

**Shield Sheldon's Reploid 5 now needs Zero or the Blade Armor.** It stands on
a ledge beside the Blade Body capsule that X cannot reach with a plain jump,
and logic called it free — so a multiworld put another stage's Access Codes on
it and there was no way to get them. Its two neighbours, Reploid 4 and the
Blade Body capsule itself, were checked at the same time and really are free.

## New option: `starting_rank`

Hunter Rank decides how many Power-up Parts you may wear, Rank is bought with
Nightmare Souls, and **X and Zero each have their own count**. Below Rank A
there are no slots at all, and the first one costs 500 of that character's own
Souls — long after a seed has handed you 24 Parts as items. This option makes
the rank you name cost nothing and leaves the ranks above it as they were.
`rank_a` is the free one (one slot each, nothing else changes); SA and above
also raise every boss's fight level, which the option text says. Off by
default.

## New option: `no_progression_behind`

Name the kinds of place the fill may not hide anything important in:
`spikes` for the Shadow Armor rooms, `movement` for what needs Zero or the
full Blade Armor, `nightmare_wall` for North Pole's ice wall, or `all`. Those
checks still exist, still need what they always did and still send their
item; they simply hold junk. The default is an empty list, which is the game
as it has always been here. Ask for more than a seed has junk to fill and
generation refuses with a message naming what to change.

## `exit_stage_anytime` now works everywhere

Another Routes, Gate's Lab and the Intro Stage included. It only ever covered
the eight Maverick stages, which is why leaving an Another Route still meant
dying on purpose. Leaving the Intro Stage early is the one case nobody has
tested.

## Also

"Nothing in this randomizer needs Souls" was wrong and the option text and
docs now say so: no check needs them, but Souls are what let you equip
anything, and `disabled_nightmare_effects` chokes the supply. The disc-option
lists in the player docs were incomplete and now name everything.

## Updating mid-seed

- The **Sheldon Reploid rule is logic**, so seeds generated before 0.3.0 keep
  the old rule. **Regenerate** to get it.
- **`exit_stage_anytime` and `starting_rank` are disc changes.** A **re-patch**
  is enough for those; the seed does not change.
- **Replace `MMX6-Unpatcher.exe`.** The disc edit list grew, and the previous
  exe does not know the new sites, so it would leave them on a disc it
  "restored".

`mmx6.apworld` goes in your Archipelago install's `custom_worlds/` folder.
`MMX6-Unpatcher.exe` restores an AP-patched disc (recoloured or not) to a clean
dump if you have lost your original — drag a `.bin` onto it.
`MMX6-Setup-Guide.pdf` is the setup guide, readable before anything is
installed.

Requires Archipelago 0.6.7 or newer. 573 tests, release gate 102/102,
packaged e2e 15/15, unpatcher round-trip verified on both accepted dumps with
every option on.

All MMX6 releases: https://github.com/Shinnuu/Archipelago/releases?q=mmx6
mmx6-v0.3.0.title: MMX6 apworld v0.3.0 (superseded by v0.3.1)

mmx6-v0.3.1.description:
Two fixes, both found in live play on 0.3.0 and both older than 0.3.0.

**Re-patch your disc. You do NOT need to regenerate.** Neither of these is a
logic change — the seeds themselves were always fine, only the way two things
were written to the disc was not. Your existing `.apmmx6` will do; just open
it again against your clean dump.

## Fixed: `boss_hp_randomization` could leave four bosses on almost no health

Blizzard Wolfang, Metal Shark Player, Shield Sheldon and Infinity Mijinion set
their HP by **adding** to a bonus that grows with your Hunter Rank, where every
other boss simply loads a number. We were patching the number, so on those four
the game went on adding the rank bonus on top of our roll — and a high roll met
at a decent rank passed the game's ceiling of 127, wrapped negative, and the
boss arrived with almost nothing. Seen in play on Infinity Mijinion.

All four now get exactly the rolled value, so the option's 32–127 range is what
you actually fight. Their vanilla per-rank scaling is gone **when they are
randomized**, which was already true of the other twelve bosses.

Two conditions had to coincide for this to show up — a high roll *and* the boss
fought above level 1 — which is why it took until now. At level 1 the bonus is
zero, which is also why every one of those sites verified as correct.

## Fixed: a starting life below 32 drew the wrong sprites

The life bar picks its picture from a list, and below a gauge of 32 it was
indexing past the front of that list into other pieces of the HUD — a stray
panel across the screen, a misplaced life count, and at very low values the
whole top-left display vanishing.

It always played fine, and it healed itself once enough upgrades carried you
back over 32 — which is why one report described the bar as fixing itself on
its own. Heart Tanks and Life Ups sent by other worlds count towards that.

The bar now stops shrinking at its smallest real size instead. **Only seeds
with `starting_hp` below 32 get this edit**; every other disc is byte-identical
to 0.3.0's.

Above 64 is deliberately unchanged: the bar runs on past the end of its own
frame, which is how most games in this genre draw a bar past its vanilla
maximum.

## What was and was not seen running

Stated plainly, as always.

**Confirmed in play:** the life bar fix, at a maximum of 8, with the patch
toggled on and off live for comparison; Heart Tanks still raising the maximum
and growing the bar; a health pickup restoring to the new maximum and stopping
there without touching it.

**Confirmed on the disc but NOT fought:** the boss HP fix. The instruction at
all 28 sites was disassembled and checked rather than sampled, the patched form
is asserted in the test suite and re-derived from a live roll in the release
gate, and the disc builds and boots — but nobody has fought a randomized
Blizzard Wolfang, Metal Shark Player, Shield Sheldon or Infinity Mijinion at a
high Hunter Rank on this build. If one of those four still dies in a couple of
hits with `boss_hp_randomization` on, please say so.

**Unchanged and still true:** a maximum below 32 cannot fill the bar
completely, because the shortest frame the game owns holds 32 and there is no
smaller artwork. The bar is correct and grows normally; it simply does not read
as full at a very low maximum.

## The three assets

- `mmx6.apworld` — drop it in your Archipelago `custom_worlds/` folder
- `MMX6-Unpatcher.exe` — restores a clean dump if you patched over your only
  copy. **Take this release's one**; it carries a manifest the older ones do
  not and will refuse discs built by this version otherwise.
- `MMX6-Setup-Guide.pdf` — the same guide that ships inside the apworld

Requires Archipelago 0.6.7 or later.
mmx6-v0.3.1.title: MMX6 apworld v0.3.1 (superseded by v0.4.0)

mmx6-v0.4.0.description:
Three new options and a logic fix.

**Regenerate your seed for this release.** The logic fix below applies to every
seed, so a re-patch alone is not enough. Everything new is off by default, so
you only need to re-patch as well if you turn one of them on.

## Fixed — regenerate

**Rainy Turtloid's Reploid 7 is behind spikes, and logic did not know.** It
carried no requirement at all, so a multiworld could put anything there —
including another player's progression — behind spikes no seed was ever told
about. It now needs the Shadow Armor, like the three Reploids either side of
it. Found in play.

Same shape as the Shield Sheldon Reploid 5 bug fixed in 0.3.0, and for the same
reason: Reploid requirements are inherited from the pickup beside them, and
this one has no pickup beside it.

## New — `stage_music`

Shuffles the music between stages. The eleven themes the stages already use are
dealt back out among them, so every stage still gets a real stage theme, every
theme is still used somewhere, and **no stage keeps the theme it started with**.

Places that share music in the base game are split, so Secret Lab 1, 2A and 2B
each get their own and the Secret Lab 3 boss rush is separated from Sigma. A
Maverick stage and its revisit stay matched, so a stage sounds the same however
often you enter it.

Only stages change — the Stage Select, menus, the Mission Report, cutscenes,
every jingle and the ending keep vanilla music. Off by default. **Changes the
disc.**

## New — `nightmare_wall_always_open`

Nine of Blizzard Wolfang's locations sit behind North Pole's ice wall, and in
the base game the only thing that opens it is Nightmare Fire being active on his
stage — which means beating Blaze Heatnix first. Those nine are the only checks
in the game with a stage-order requirement. Turn this on and the wall is never
in your way.

**Expect fire in that room.** The test this forces does not only gate the wall,
it selects how the room is set up — so the room runs its Fire-afflicted
version, hazards and all. That is the room exactly as the base game presents
it, since Fire being on is the only way anyone gets in there. Your Nightmare
Effect state is untouched.

Off by default. **Changes the disc, and changes logic** — regenerate if you
turn it on.

## New goal — `all_mavericks_high_max_sigma`

All eight Mavericks **and** High Max, then Sigma. Gate's Lab stays shut until
both are done.

High Max is the second Another Route boss, so reaching him means clearing one
route first — the Zero Nightmare — which hands you Zero whether or not
`zero_unlock` put him in the pool.

This goal cannot be spoiled by the base game's missable-boss problem: once
Gate's Lab opens High Max is gone from that file for good, so a goal that merely
*asked* for him could be made impossible by opening the lab first. Here the lab
cannot open until he is dead. **Changes the disc.**

## Renamed

`all_mavericks` is now **`all_mavericks_sigma`** — it always did require beating
Sigma afterwards and the old name did not say so. **Your existing YAML keeps
working**: the old name is kept as an alias and the stored value is unchanged.

## Assets

- `mmx6.apworld` — drop in `custom_worlds/`
- `MMX6-Unpatcher.exe` — restores an AP-patched disc to your clean dump, if you
  patched over your only copy. Rebuilt for this release; the previous build
  cannot restore a disc patched with any of these three options.
- `MMX6-Setup-Guide.pdf` — start here if you have not played an Archipelago
  seed of this before.

## Verified

695 tests, a 110-check release gate, and a 15-step end-to-end through the
packaged apworld — template, generation, Open Patch, and the unpatcher round
trip on both accepted disc dumps.

Played, not just tested: the ice wall was walked through with Blaze Heatnix
unbeaten, the new goal was exercised across its whole truth table (each half
alone leaves the lab shut, both together open it), and the music shuffle was
confirmed in a running game.

## Not verified

- No seed generated through Archipelago with `stage_music: true` has been
  played by a human. The packaged path is covered by the end-to-end test.
- The Secret Lab music rows are correct on the disc and in RAM, but nobody has
  played them.
- The ice-wall check exists in four overlay copies; all four are patched and
  byte-verified, but only one has been watched executing.
